document.title: A/S Inderfurth and S/CT Sheehan Meet Taliban Representatives (Islama 00567)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] Karl Inderfurth and Michael Sheehan meet Taliban officials Amir Khan Muttaqi and Ambassador Syed Mohammad Haqqani for two hours. No progress on bin Laden, but the Taliban agree that hijacking is a terrorist act and say they have always condemned terrorism. Excised.

events.description: Two-hour meeting of Inderfurth, Sheehan and US officials with Taliban reps Muttaqi and Haqqani on hijacking, bin Ladin, UNSCR 1267 and peace.
Indian Airways hijacking, plane taken to Kandahar; one killed, three prisoners freed, hijackers escaped.
Cable sent from US Embassy Islamabad to State Department reporting the meeting.
Inderfurth and Sheehan met Taliban representatives led by Muttaqi; Sheehan pressed for implementation of the UN resolution on bin Ladin and Inderfurth urged peace talks.
Embassy Islamabad sent cable 00567 reporting the meeting with Taliban representatives.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reports the Inderfurth/Sheehan meeting with Taliban representatives, covering the ulema conference and bin Ladin's status.
Sheehan told the Taliban the US would support an ulema conference only as a means to comply with the UNSCR, not as a substitute.
Muttaqi repeated three Taliban proposals on bin Ladin: an Afghan court trial, an ulema conference, or OIC supervision; he said the US rejected all.
Sheehan told the Taliban the US has evidence bin Ladin is planning terrorist acts and urged them to act soon.
Inderfurth outlined the Pakistan-Iran initiative for a ceasefire and talks among four parties with the UN, and US support for a loya jirga.
Inderfurth and Sheehan met Taliban representatives Muttaqi and Haqqani in Islamabad for two hours, discussing the Indian Airways hijacking, bin Ladin and UNSCR 1267.
Indian Airways plane hijacked; landed in Kandahar after stops at Amritsar, Lahore and Dubai; one passenger killed; three prisoners freed; hijackers escaped.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting the meeting sent to State Department.
Arrest of a cell in Jordan linked to bin Ladin's people planning an attack.
Sheehan's recent telephone conversation with Taliban foreign minister Muttawakil on bin Ladin and UNSCR 1267.

relationships.detail: Taliban director for administration of Council of Ministers, chief of cabinet equivalent.
relationships.quote: MUTTAQI WAS EQUIVALENT TO THE CHIEF OF CABINET FOR THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Taliban ambassador to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN AMBASSADOR TO PAKISTAN SYED MOHAMMAD HAQQANI

relationships.detail: Met at Islamabad on 20 Jan 2000.
relationships.quote: MET FOR TWO HOURS ON JANUARY 20 WITH TALIBAN DIRECTOR FOR ADMINISTRATION

relationships.detail: Urged compliance with UNSCR 1267 and expulsion of bin Ladin.
relationships.quote: WE ENCOURAGE YOU TO FIND A WAY TO COMPLY WITH UNSCR 1267 AND EXPEL BIN LADIN TO JUSTICE

relationships.detail: Earlier telephone conversation on bin Ladin and UNSCR 1267.
relationships.quote: WHAT HE HAD DISCUSSED WITH THEIR FOREIGN MINISTER TELEPHONICALLY

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin has been in Afghanistan for years under Taliban; US will hold Taliban responsible.
relationships.quote: THE U.S. WILL HOLD THE TALIBAN RESPONSIBLE IF HE COMMITS ANY FURTHER

relationships.detail: Referred to as head of 'his organization' / 'his network'.
relationships.quote: BIN LADIN CANNOT COMMUNICATE WITH HIS ORGANIZATION TO GIVE COMMANDS

relationships.detail: Previously met in Kabul during Richardson visit.
relationships.quote: HE HAD MET INDERFURTH IN KABUL

relationships.detail: Translator for Taliban delegation.
relationships.quote: AND TRANSLATOR NAIM DINDAR

relationships.detail: Sheehan urged the Taliban delegation to find a way to implement the UN resolution on bin Ladin, saying the U.S. has evidence he is planning terrorism.
relationships.quote: I ENCOURAGE YOU IN ALL SINCERITY AND FRIENDSHIP TO FIND A WAY TO RESOLVE THIS SOON.

relationships.detail: Sheehan said the U.S. has evidence bin Ladin is planning acts of terrorism despite Taliban claims he cannot communicate with his network.
relationships.quote: WE HAVE EVIDENCE HE IS PLANNING ACTS OF TERRORISM.

relationships.detail: The U.S. pressed the Taliban to act on bin Ladin, who is under Taliban restrictions and whom the U.S. wants brought to justice.
relationships.quote: EVEN IF BIN LADIN IS UNDER SOME RESTRICTIONS, TWO ISSUES REMAIN.

relationships.detail: Inderfurth urged the Taliban to cooperate with a peace initiative and meet expatriate Afghan representatives.
relationships.quote: THE U.S. SUPPORTS THIS INITIATIVE, INDERFURTH SAID, AND HOPES THE TALIBAN WILL COOPERATE.

relationships.detail: Inderfurth described a planned cease-fire followed by talks among the four parties and with the UN for a broader resolution.
relationships.quote: TALKS AMONG THE FOUR PARTIES AND WITH THE UNITED NATIONS TO BRING A BROADER RESOLUTION OF THE CONFLICT.

relationships.detail: Muttaqi concluded the meeting speaking for the Taliban delegation.
relationships.quote: CONCLUDING FOR THE TALIBAN DELEGATION, MUTTAQI STATED THAT THE TALIBAN WILL WORK FOR PEACE.

relationships.detail: Muttaqi hoped the delegations could meet again to discuss rehabilitation.
relationships.quote: MUTTAQI EXPRESSED THE HOPE THAT SOMEDAY THE DELEGATIONS COULD MEET TO DISCUSS REHABILITATION.

relationships.detail: Inderfurth and Sheehan jointly cleared the cable on the meeting.
relationships.quote: A/S INDERFURTH AND S/CT SHEEHAN CLEARED THIS CABLE.

relationships.detail: Milam, signing as Ambassador, sent the cable from Embassy Islamabad to State.
relationships.quote: MILAM

relationships.detail: Sheehan pressed Muttaqi on Taliban compliance with the UN resolution and on the ulema conference proposal.
relationships.quote: MUTTAQI IMMEDIATELY ASKED IF SHEEHAN WERE SAYING THE U.S. AGREED TO THE ULEMA IDEA.

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin was present in Afghanistan, which Muttaqi said harmed Taliban relations with the world.
relationships.quote: THE MERE EXISTENCE OF BIN LADIN IN AFGHANISTAN HAS CAUSED TALIBAN RELATIONS WITH THE WHOLE WORLD TO DETERIORATE

relationships.detail: The Taliban were subject to UN sanctions and a Security Council resolution (UNSCR) demanding bin Ladin's surrender; the Taliban objected to the sanctions.
relationships.quote: AFGHANS EXPECTED THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY TO HELP, NOT MAKE MATTERS WORSE WITH SANCTIONS.

relationships.detail: The Taliban proposed supervision of bin Ladin by the OIC as one of three ways to resolve the issue.
relationships.quote: SUPERVISION OF UBL BY THE ORGANIZATION OF ISLAMIC CONFERENCE (OIC)

relationships.detail: Muttaqi said the Taliban spoke with the Jordanian Embassy about those arrested, who he claimed were only involved in the Afghan jihad.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD SPOKEN WITH THE JORDANIAN EMBASSY AND THOSE ARRESTED WERE ONLY INVOLVED IN THE AFGHAN JIHAD

relationships.detail: Muttaqi referred to bin Ladin's organization, claiming he cannot communicate with it to give commands.
relationships.quote: BIN LADIN CANNOT COMMUNICATE WITH HIS ORGANIZATION TO GIVE COMMANDS.

relationships.detail: Inderfurth and Sheehan met Taliban representatives in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: INDERFURTH NOTED THAT THE U.S. REMAINS THE LARGEST HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE DONOR TO AFGHANISTAN.

relationships.detail: Sheehan and Inderfurth jointly delegated to the Taliban meeting and made joint US points.
relationships.quote: THEY POINTED OUT THAT THE U.S. HAS NO DESIGNS ON AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: The Indian Airways hijacking, which the US was concerned was successful, targeted India.
relationships.quote: THE U.S. IS SO CONCERNED THAT THE INDIAN AIRWAYS HIJACKING WAS SUCCESSFUL

relationships.detail: The Taliban governed the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: SINCE THE FOUNDING OF THE ISLAMIC EMIRATE OF AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Sheehan met Muttaqi at the January 20 meeting in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: MET FOR TWO HOURS ON JANUARY 20 WITH TALIBAN DIRECTOR FOR ADMINISTRATION, COUNCIL OF MINISTERS, AMIR KHAN MUTTAQI

relationships.detail: Inderfurth met Taliban ambassador Haqqani at the January 20 meeting.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN AMBASSADOR TO PAKISTAN SYED MOHAMMAD HAQQANI, AND TRANSLATOR NAIM DINDAR

relationships.detail: Sheehan met Haqqani at the January 20 meeting.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN AMBASSADOR TO PAKISTAN SYED MOHAMMAD HAQQANI

relationships.detail: Haqqani remembered meeting Inderfurth in Kabul when Inderfurth accompanied Bill Richardson.
relationships.quote: HAQQANI REMEMBERED THAT HE HAD MET INDERFURTH IN KABUL WHEN THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY ACCOMPANIED THEN UN-AMBASSADOR BILL RICHARDSON

relationships.detail: Inderfurth accompanied Richardson (then UN ambassador) on a visit to Kabul.
relationships.quote: WHEN THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY ACCOMPANIED THEN UN-AMBASSADOR BILL RICHARDSON

relationships.detail: Muttaqi is Taliban director for administration of the Council of Ministers and former information minister.
relationships.quote: MUTTAQI, THE TALIBAN'S FORMER INFORMATION MINISTER, FLEW FROM AFGHANISTAN FOR THE MEETING.

relationships.detail: Haqqani serves as Taliban ambassador to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN AMBASSADOR TO PAKISTAN SYED MOHAMMAD HAQQANI

relationships.detail: Dindar translated for the Taliban delegation.
relationships.quote: AND TRANSLATOR NAIM DINDAR

relationships.detail: Muttawakil is Taliban foreign minister.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN FOREIGN MINISTER MUTTAWAKIL

relationships.detail: Sheehan had a recent (telephone) conversation with Muttawakil about bin Ladin and UNSCR 1267.
relationships.quote: WHAT HE HAD DISCUSSED WITH THEIR FOREIGN MINISTER TELEPHONICALLY -- USAMA BIN LADIN AND UNSCR 1267

relationships.detail: Camp is NSC Director for South Asia.
relationships.quote: NSC DIRECTOR FOR SOUTH ASIA CAMP

relationships.detail: Inderfurth is Assistant Secretary for South Asia.
relationships.quote: SA ASSISTANT SECRETARY INDERFURTH

relationships.detail: Sheehan is Coordinator for Counterterrorism (S/CT).
relationships.quote: S/CT AMBASSADOR SHEEHAN

relationships.detail: Bibbins is S/CT special assistant.
relationships.quote: S/CT SPECIAL ASSISTANT BIBBINS

relationships.detail: Milam is the US Ambassador in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: AMBASSADOR MILAM AND POLOFF (NOTETAKER)

relationships.detail: US says Taliban have hosted bin Ladin in Afghanistan for years, so they would be held responsible for his acts.
relationships.quote: WHEN A PERSON HAS A CRIMINAL IN HIS HOUSE FOR SEVERAL YEARS, AND THAT CRIMINAL CONDUCTS TERRORIST ACTS FROM THE HOUSE

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin has been in Afghanistan a long time.
relationships.quote: BECAUSE BIN LADIN HAS BEEN IN AFGHANISTAN SO LONG

relationships.detail: Sheehan urged Taliban to comply with UNSCR 1267 and expel bin Ladin.
relationships.quote: WE ENCOURAGE YOU TO FIND A WAY TO COMPLY WITH UNSCR 1267 AND EXPEL BIN LADIN TO JUSTICE.

relationships.detail: Sheehan believes Taliban are not coordinating terrorist activities with bin Ladin.
relationships.quote: THEY ARE NOT COORDINATING TERRORIST ACTIVITIES WITH BIN LADIN

relationships.detail: Taliban released the hijackers after assurances from India and UN; US says Taliban let them escape.
relationships.quote: THE HIJACKERS WERE RELEASED ONLY AFTER THE TALIBAN RECEIVED THE AGREEMENT OF THE GOI AND THE UN

relationships.detail: The hijacked plane landed at Kandahar where hijackers achieved their ends.
relationships.quote: IT WAS IN KANDAHAR -- NOT KABUL OR HERAT OR OTHER LOCATIONS -- WHERE THE HIJACKERS STOOD THE BEST CHANCE

relationships.detail: Taliban allowed the plane to land after written agreement from India.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN ONLY ALLOWED THE PLANE TO LAND AFTER RECEIVING WRITTEN AGREEMENT FROM THE GOVERNMENT OF INDIA.

relationships.detail: UN and Indian negotiators promised hijackers would not be arrested in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: HIJACKERS HAD BEEN PROMISED BY UN AND INDIAN NEGOTIATORS THAT THEY WOULD NOT BE ARRESTED IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin's people plan and conduct terrorist activities, evidenced by arrest of a cell in Jordan.
relationships.quote: BIN LADIN'S PEOPLE CONTINUE TO PLAN AND CONDUCT TERRORIST ACTIVITIES, WITH THE ARREST OF A CELL IN JORDAN

relationships.detail: A cell linked to bin Ladin's people was arrested in Jordan.
relationships.quote: WITH THE ARREST OF A CELL IN JORDAN PROVIDING THE MOST RECENT PROOF

relationships.detail: Muttaqi asked whether the US agreed to the Taliban ulema conference idea as route to compliance with UNSCR 1267.
relationships.quote: MUTTAQI IMMEDIATELY ASKED IF SHEEHAN WERE SAYING THE U.S. AGREED TO THE ULEMA IDEA.

key_claims: The US judged the Taliban had no part in arranging the Indian Airways hijacking but faulted them for letting hijackers escape.
Sheehan said the US believed the Taliban were not coordinating terrorist activities with bin Ladin, though his people continued to plan attacks, citing a Jordan cell arrest.
The US said it would hold the Taliban responsible for any further acts by bin Ladin.
Muttaqi said bin Ladin cannot communicate with his organization and proposed an Afghan trial, ulema conference or OIC supervision.
The US would accept an ulema conference only as cover for compliance with UNSCR 1267, not as a substitute.
Muttaqi said bin Ladin's presence damaged Taliban relations worldwide and that Taliban reflect popular will.
Inderfurth backed a Pakistan-Iran ceasefire initiative and an expatriate-led loya jirga.
